chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said:

A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) claiming a debt against al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, and said, 'He has taken my right.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'He has taken your right which killed him.' Then he said to al-Wid, 'Stand up to the man and pay him from your own wealth, for I want his skin to cool, even if it is already cool.'

key_terms.الْمُعَلَّى بْنِ خُنَيْسٍ: al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays (a companion of the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Imam's statement 'He has taken your right which killed him' regarding al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Imam’s pragmatic approach to debt settlement, prioritizing the creditor’s emotional satisfaction ('cooling the skin') over strict legal technicalities. It highlights the virtue of *Ihsan* (excellence in conduct) and the spiritual merit of paying off debts on behalf of martyrs, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on social harmony and financial responsibility.
